title: 1991 AHSME Problem 12
statement: The measures (in degrees) of the interior angles of a convex hexagon form an arithmetic sequence of positive integers. Let \(m^\circ\) be the measure of the largest interior angle of the hexagon. The largest possible value of \(m^\circ\) is

solutions.text:
The angle sum is \(720^\circ,\) so \[ \begin{aligned} 6a+15d&=720,\\ 2a+5d&=240. \end{aligned} \] Hence \(d\) is even. The largest angle is \(a+5d=120+\frac52d,\) which must be less than \(180.\) Thus \(d\lt24,\) and the largest allowable even value is \(d=22.\) It gives \(a=65\) and \(m=65+5(22)=175.\)

Thus the correct answer is D.
hints: Write the angles as \(a,a+d,\ldots,a+5d\) and use their sum
The equation forces \(d\) to be even, and convexity bounds the largest angle below \(180^\circ\)
